title: agent-fork Phase 3 — design decisions (D2–D14)
lead: Thirteen pick-one decisions. Each opens with context and a ★ recommendation — recommendations are pre-selected, so change any you disagree with, add notes, then Export → MD (or click “Here are my answers”) and paste the result back into chat.

sections.title: What should a bare fork carry over by default?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D3. This sets the defaults everything else builds on.

choices.label: Exact-copy: carry staged + unstaged + untracked (gitignored stays off)
choices.detail: Comprehensive by default — the fork continues your in-flight work; tweak down with flags.

choices.label: Clean-from-HEAD: worktree at the parent's commit, no uncommitted state
choices.detail: Minimal by default — carrying state becomes an opt-in flag.

sections.title: How should the state choice appear in flags and config?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D2. Defines the flag vocabulary and config keys.

choices.label: agent-deck toggles: --no-with-state / --with-ignored flags, with_state / with_ignored config keys
choices.detail: One vocabulary, direct port of the proven schema; flag↔env↔config name parity is trivial.

choices.label: A named mode: --clean flag, mode = "exact" | "clean" in config
choices.detail: Fewer flags on the happy path, but a second vocabulary for the same axis — and --with-ignored still exists.

choices.label: Toggles canonical plus --clean as a documented alias for --no-with-state
choices.detail: Both vocabularies from day one.

sections.title: Where should the fork's worktree directory land?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D5. A worktree_location config override exists in every variant.

choices.label: Sibling dir <repo>-<branch-slug>; mirror the parent's pattern when the parent is itself a worktree
choices.detail: agent-deck's default plus the kickoff's mirror rule for already-forked parents.

choices.label: Sibling dir always — no mirroring heuristic
choices.detail: Simplest predictable rule; nested forks may land somewhere surprising.

choices.label: Central forks dir under XDG data (~/.local/share/agent-fork/worktrees/<repo>/…)
choices.detail: Keeps project parents clean, but hides working code far from the repo.

choices.label: Inside the repo: <repo>/.worktrees/<branch-slug>
choices.detail: agent-deck's 'subdirectory' option; keeps everything under one root.

sections.title: Where does a fork's name come from?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D4. The name seeds the branch slug, worktree suffix, and session name.

choices.label: Optional positional (agent-fork fork fix-auth); auto-derived from branch + date when omitted
choices.detail: Auto form: <parent-branch-slug>-<mmdd>, collisions suffixed -2, -3 (agent-deck's scheme).

choices.label: Required positional — a name must always be given
choices.detail: Always explicit, but breaks the zero-argument one-word flow.

choices.label: Always auto-generated — no name argument accepted
choices.detail: Zero decisions at fork time, zero control.

sections.title: What display name does the forked session get?

choices.label: The fork name itself — one identity across branch, worktree, and session
choices.detail: "fix-auth-2" is the branch suffix, the directory suffix, and the session you pick in /resume.

choices.label: A parent-derived template like {parent}-fork-{n}
choices.detail: Richer lineage, but the parent's display name is not reliably discoverable (env exposes only its id).

choices.label: No name — let the agent use its default
choices.detail: Loses findability in session pickers.

sections.title: What should happen when a native session fork is impossible?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D14. Applies when preflight finds an old CLI, a missing Codex rollout, or an unrelated directory.

choices.label: Degradation ladder: native fork, else fresh NAMED session + generated HANDOFF.md seeded via the launch command
choices.detail: Preflight picks the rung before emitting; the handoff carries parent id, anchor commit, branch, status snapshot, and a task-notes slot the skill fills.

choices.label: Refuse with a diagnosis — no fallback rung in v1
choices.detail: Simplest and honest, but old-CLI users get nothing.

choices.label: The ladder plus a third rung: copy the Claude session file into the target project dir
choices.detail: Manipulates a format Anthropic declares internal and version-unstable; research verdict was last-resort-only.

sections.title: Should fork verification run by default?

choices.label: On by default; --no-verify to skip
choices.detail: A handful of git status/rev-parse calls — milliseconds — and a failed check rolls the fork back.

choices.label: Off by default; --verify to enable (agent-deck parity)
choices.detail: agent-deck verifies only in its test suite, never at runtime.

sections.title: Should the paste command land on the clipboard in v1?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D9 (the kickoff's stretch goal).

choices.label: Yes — a --copy flag (config default off); OSC52 first, then pbcopy/xclip; failure is a notice, never an error
choices.detail: OSC52 writes the clipboard through SSH and tmux; shell-outs are the fallback.

choices.label: Defer clipboard entirely to v1.1
choices.detail: Keeps v1 lean; the command still prints on stdout.

choices.label: Copy by default when on a TTY, with --no-copy to opt out
choices.detail: One less keystroke, but a silent clipboard write surprises people.

sections.title: Should v1 ship an agent-fork list command?

choices.label: Yes — read the fork registry; show name, branch, worktree, agent, and whether the worktree still exists
choices.detail: The registry exists anyway for cleanup ownership; list is a thin read.

choices.label: Defer — git worktree list covers it for now
choices.detail: One less command, but cleanup targeting goes blind.

sections.title: What may cleanup remove, and what stops it?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D12. Consent (--yes) is separate from guards in every variant.

choices.label: Registry-scoped: only forks agent-fork created; --force extends to any worktree AND overrides the dirty/unpushed guards
choices.detail: Guards: uncommitted changes; commits on no remote (no upstream counts as unpushed); target is your current directory.

choices.label: Any worktree from the start, with the same guards everywhere
choices.detail: More useful as a general tool, more dangerous on worktrees it didn't make.

choices.label: Registry-only, permanently — --force never extends the target set
choices.detail: Safest; orphaned or hand-made worktrees need manual git.

sections.title: What is the removal command called?

choices.label: cleanup — the kickoff name (stays the one waived SHOULD in CONFORMANCE.md)
choices.detail: Does more than delete: worktree + branch + prune + registry update.

choices.label: delete — the CLI standard's core verb (drops the waiver)
choices.detail: Standard-pure; slightly undersells the multi-step semantics.

choices.label: prune — docker-style
choices.detail: Usually implies sweep-all-stale rather than remove-this-one; could later be cleanup --all instead.

sections.title: How much configuration should v1 expose?
sections.lead: Pick one — decision D7. File locations and precedence are already fixed by the CLI standard; this is only about which keys exist.

choices.label: Trimmed schema tracking today's answers: with_state, with_ignored, branch_prefix, worktree_location, verify, copy
choices.detail: Every key mirrors a flag decided above; drops agent-deck's docker, worktree toggle, and inherit_from_parent.

choices.label: Minimal: branch_prefix only — everything else is flags
choices.detail: Leanest possible; users re-type preferences per invocation.

choices.label: Full agent-deck [fork] port including inherit_from_parent
choices.detail: Maximum familiarity; carries keys with no meaning in a standalone CLI.

sections.title: Should per-agent extra-args passthrough ship in v1?

choices.label: Defer to v1.1 — keep v1's launch templates fixed and testable
choices.detail: Adding [agents.claude] extra_args later is additive and non-breaking.

choices.label: Ship in v1: [agents.<name>] extra_args injected into emitted commands
choices.detail: Power users get --model etc. now; adds a quoting/injection surface to v1.

contexts.summary: Whether the one-word fork carries your dirty working state or starts clean at the parent's commit.
contexts.recommendation: Exact-copy — the tool exists to continue in-flight work; a clean worktree at the parent's commit is what plain git worktree add already gives you. Gitignored files stay off by default either way (agent-deck flipped that default off after real-world pain: secrets in .env and unbounded node_modules-style trees).

contexts.summary: The vocabulary for exact-copy vs clean: independent toggles (agent-deck's shape) or a named mode flag.
contexts.recommendation: The agent-deck toggles — one vocabulary, a proven schema with tri-state semantics (explicit false honored), and trivial flag/env/config name parity. A --clean alias can be added compatibly later if ergonomics demand it.

contexts.summary: Where the new working directory is created relative to the repo.
contexts.recommendation: Sibling with mirror-parent — sibling <repo>-<branch> is agent-deck's default and matches how worktrees are commonly laid out by hand; the mirror rule keeps fork-of-fork placement consistent with whatever pattern the parent already follows.

contexts.summary: Whether the fork's name is given, derived, or both.
contexts.recommendation: Optional positional with an auto-derived fallback — preserves the zero-argument flow (the skill can always call it bare) while letting a human name the fork when the name matters. agent-deck derives from the session title; with no title available, branch + date is the deterministic equivalent.

contexts.summary: The name the forked session shows in its agent's session picker and terminal title.
contexts.recommendation: Use the fork name — one identity across branch, worktree, and session keeps the mental model flat, and it needs no discovery machinery. Parent-derived templates require reading the parent's display name, which the environment does not expose.

contexts.summary: The behavior when preflight determines a native session fork cannot work.
contexts.recommendation: The two-rung ladder — never emit a command known to fail, and degrade to a fresh named session seeded with a generated handoff file so the user still gets a working fork of their code with context to continue from. Leave the session-file-copy trick out of v1: it manipulates a format its vendor declares unstable.

contexts.summary: Whether the fork is checked against its contract at runtime or assumed correct from exit codes.
contexts.recommendation: On by default with --no-verify — the checks cost milliseconds, agent-deck documents this exact contract but never enforces it at runtime, and a tool whose output is a paste-command should not hand over an unverified fork.

contexts.summary: Whether and how the emitted paste command reaches the clipboard.
contexts.recommendation: Ship it as an explicit --copy flag with OSC52 first — cheap to build, works over SSH/tmux, and explicit beats a silent default side effect. Config can flip it on permanently for those who want it.

contexts.summary: Whether v1 can enumerate the forks it has created.
contexts.recommendation: Yes — the state registry already exists for cleanup ownership, list is a thin read over it, and without it cleanup targeting is guesswork.

contexts.summary: The blast-radius rules for the destructive command.
contexts.recommendation: Registry-scoped with --force as the deliberate escalation — safe by default on exactly the things agent-fork made, while still giving an operator a way to clean up anything, consistent with the standard's force-overrides-guards semantics.
Keep cleanup — it is the kickoff's name, its semantics are broader than delete, and the conformance waiver is already recorded. Rename later only if the waiver ever grates.

contexts.summary: Which config keys exist in v1.
contexts.recommendation: The trimmed schema — every key mirrors a flag decided above (nothing config-only), and the three agent-deck keys with no standalone meaning (docker, the worktree toggle, inherit_from_parent) stay dropped.

contexts.summary: Whether users can inject extra CLI arguments into the emitted launch commands.
contexts.recommendation: Defer — v1's templates stay fixed strings that tests can assert byte-for-byte; passthrough is additive later and carries a quoting/injection surface better designed once real requests exist.
